scenario: A gallery curator is scheduling five paintings—Acacia, Birch, Cedar, Dogwood, and Elm—to be hung in five consecutive wall positions numbered 1 through 5 from left to right. Each painting will be displayed in one of two lighting conditions: either under warm lighting or under cool lighting. Each position has exactly one painting, and each painting is displayed in exactly one lighting condition.

rules.description: Acacia is hung in position 1 under warm lighting.
If Dogwood is in position 5, then Dogwood is displayed under cool lighting.
Cedar and Dogwood are not hung in adjacent positions.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the complete list of paintings from position 1 to position 5, along with their lighting conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acacia (warm), Birch (cool), Elm (warm), Cedar (warm), Dogwood (cool)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acacia (warm), Birch (warm), Cedar (warm), Dogwood (warm), Elm (cool)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acacia (warm), Elm (warm), Birch (cool), Cedar (warm), Dogwood (warm)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acacia (warm), Birch (warm), Cedar (warm), Elm (cool), Dogwood (warm)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acacia (cool), Birch (warm), Cedar (warm), Dogwood (warm), Elm (warm)

explanations.correct: Acacia is in position 1 under warm lighting (✓). Birch is in position 2 (✓). Cedar (position 3) is before Elm (position 5) (✓). Cedar and Dogwood are not adjacent—Cedar is in position 3, Dogwood is in position 5 (✓). Dogwood is in position 5 under cool lighting, which satisfies the conditional rule (✓). All rules satisfied.
explanations.B: Elm is in position 5, not position 4. Cedar is in position 3, Elm in position 5, satisfying 'Cedar before Elm.' However, the list shows Elm (cool) in position 5, which violates the constraint that Elm should be in the arrangement. This choice violates position assignments.
explanations.C: Birch must be in position 2, not position 3. This violates the fixed rule.
explanations.D: Elm is in position 4, but Cedar is in position 3. The rule requires Cedar before Elm, which is satisfied. However, Cedar is in position 3 and Dogwood should be in position 5, but this choice puts Elm in position 4 and Dogwood missing. The list is incomplete.
explanations.E: Acacia must be under warm lighting in position 1, not cool lighting. This violates the fixed rule.

questions.questionStem: Acacia must be displayed under which one of the following lighting conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: warm lighting

choices.label: B
choices.text: cool lighting

choices.label: C
choices.text: either warm or cool lighting, depending on the arrangement

choices.label: D
choices.text: the same lighting as Birch

choices.label: E
choices.text: the same lighting as Cedar

explanations.correct: The rule states Acacia is hung in position 1 under warm lighting. All verified solutions show Acacia under warm lighting. Acacia must be under warm lighting.
explanations.A: Correct. Acacia is fixed to warm lighting.
explanations.B: Acacia is never under cool lighting in any valid arrangement.
explanations.C: Acacia's lighting is fixed; there is no flexibility.
explanations.D: Birch can be under either warm or cool lighting, but Acacia is always warm. They are not necessarily the same.
explanations.E: Cedar can be under either warm or cool lighting, but Acacia is always warm. They are not necessarily the same.

questions.questionStem: If Cedar is displayed under warm lighting, which one of the following must be true?

localRules.description: Cedar is displayed under warm lighting.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elm is displayed under warm lighting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dogwood is displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Birch is displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elm is displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dogwood is displayed under warm lighting.

explanations.correct: When Cedar is under warm lighting, examining the verified solutions: all arrangements with Cedar in position 3 or 4 under warm lighting show that there are valid solutions where Dogwood can be warm or cool. However, checking all solutions where Cedar is warm: they include arrangements where Dogwood is in various positions. The consistent pattern across all such solutions is that Dogwood's lighting varies. Upon careful review of the verified solutions with Cedar warm, Dogwood appears under cool in some and warm in others. Actually, reviewing the verified solutions more carefully: solutions 1, 3, 7, 9 have Cedar warm. In solution 1, Dogwood is warm. In solution 3, Dogwood is warm. In solution 7, Dogwood is cool. In solution 9, Dogwood is cool. So Dogwood is not forced. Let me recalculate: Upon examination of solutions where Cedar is warm (solutions with Cedar position 3 or 4 warm): The variable that remains consistent across these scenarios is that at least one of Elm or Dogwood must satisfy certain constraints. Given the conditional rule about Dogwood in position 5, when Cedar is warm and Dogwood is in position 5, Dogwood must be cool. This creates a forced relationship. Actually, the answer marked here requires solver re-verification. The question is flagged.
explanations.A: Elm can be under either warm or cool lighting when Cedar is warm.
explanations.B: Dogwood can be under either warm or cool lighting when Cedar is warm.
explanations.C: Birch can be under either warm or cool lighting when Cedar is warm.
explanations.D: Elm can be under either warm or cool lighting when Cedar is warm.
explanations.E: This requires solver verification; please see criticNotes.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following cannot be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acacia and Birch are both displayed under warm lighting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cedar and Elm are both displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dogwood is displayed under cool lighting and positioned in position 5.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cedar is positioned in position 4 and displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Birch is displayed under warm lighting and Cedar is displayed under cool lighting.

explanations.correct: Examining the verified solutions: in every single valid arrangement, at least one of Cedar or Elm is displayed under warm lighting. There is no solution where both Cedar and Elm are under cool lighting. This is because of the ordering constraint (Cedar before Elm) and the lighting distribution across the gallery.
explanations.A: Acacia is always warm and Birch can be warm—this is true in solutions 1, 3, 4, 7.
explanations.B: Correct. No verified solution has both Cedar and Elm under cool lighting.
explanations.C: Dogwood in position 5 under cool lighting appears in multiple solutions (solutions 2, 7, 8, 9, 10).
explanations.D: Cedar in position 4 under cool lighting appears in solution 9.
explanations.E: Birch warm and Cedar cool appears in solutions 1 and 3.

questions.questionStem: If Dogwood is positioned in position 4, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cedar is positioned in position 3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elm is positioned in position 5.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Birch is displayed under cool lighting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cedar is displayed under warm lighting.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elm is displayed under warm lighting.

explanations.correct: When Dogwood is in position 4, the remaining positions are 3 and 5 for Cedar and Elm. Since Cedar must be before Elm, Cedar must be in position 3 and Elm in position 5. All solutions with Dogwood in position 4 (solutions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) confirm that Elm is always in position 5 when Dogwood is in position 4.
explanations.A: Cedar is indeed in position 3 when Dogwood is in position 4, but see criticNotes.
explanations.B: Correct. When Dogwood is in position 4, Cedar must be in position 3 and Elm must be in position 5.
explanations.C: Birch can be under either warm or cool lighting.
explanations.D: Cedar can be under either warm or cool lighting.
explanations.E: Elm can be under either warm or cool lighting.
